parsed.why: Upheld 14-year sodomy statute, routine police detention and extortion of gender-nonconforming people with no working remedy, hostile social climate; offset by expanding court protections and no trans-specific offence or organised targeting.

Self-ID framework, identity-based facility access, official tolerance advice, and documented enforcement of the transphobia aggravation with convictions; only conservative attitudes outside big cities and one region's resident-facing repeals remain.

Enforced statute used to arrest trans people on gender expression, forced genital display and public humiliation by police, official and religious hostility, blocked organisations, no protections or recourse; society largely unaccepting.

Police raids, collective detentions and public shaming, documented sexual violence against trans women in custody, legacy vagrancy law applied, rape laws unenforced, state repression of LGBT advocacy with no gender-identity protection.

Strong visitor-facing protections and working courts, but patterned lethal violence against trans women with limited accountability and armed-group kill lists naming trans people in named departments; cities markedly safer than conflict regions.
